newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi share index down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi share index down in slow trading.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index eased on Tuesday, pulled down by price losses in a few counters in a slow trading session, brokers said.
The index fell 0.19 points to stand at 3064.21 while the turnover was posted at 7.660 million shillings on 294,436 shares from 8.890 million shillings on 364,108 shares on Monday.
"Tuesday's trading session was quite slow as only small volumes were traded in most counters. Price ranges fluctuated," a bourse official said.
Brokers said there was not much activity in the market. They added that most counters were depressed and pointed to the agricultural sector where only Rea Vipingo Plantations Ltd was traded.
"This is because there are very many small shareholders in the counter who have been in the market for long and they are both willing buyers and sellers for the stock," a dealer said.
Rea Vipingo traded 16,850 shares at 11.20 from 11.

One broker said that it seemed most investors were waiting on the sideline for Kenya Commercial Bank to begin trading 11.88 million primary shares when the government offloads another 10 percent of its holding in the bank.
That will happen between September 16 and October 15.
Kenya Commercial Bank remained steady at 55, National Bank of Kenya eased to 18 from 18.20 on 57,975 shares while Housing Finance Company of Kenya fell to 25 from 26.

The Nation Printers & Publishers Monday announcement of profit before tax of 162.2 million shillings for the six months to June 1996 had little effect on the share price which saw only a marginal increase.
Nation Printers rose to 104 from 103, Kenya Airways traded at 11.50, 11 and 11.20 on 108,459 shares while Uchumi Supermarket was dealt unchanged at 39.
Bourse officials said that foreign investors dealt 38,000 shares of National Industrial Credit at 41 shillings and 65,000 of Kenya Airways at 11.50.
